A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TRACT and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D. Retained material can be matched reliably despite additions and relocation in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, ablations, inference-scaling experiments, and CoT quality and perplexity analyses in Sections 5–6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CLoud comparisons and RewardBench results in Section 7 and Table 10.

M1.justification: The CoT-RAFT objective, CoT-RAIL predictor, self-generated training data construction, and two-stage initialization procedure remain unchanged in Equations 1–4 and Algorithm 1. RewardBench evaluates the existing score predictors.

E1.justification: v2 retains Feedback Collection training and the four original pointwise benchmarks, while adding RewardBench. This substantially extends evaluation to pairwise preference selection across Chat, Chat-Hard, Safety, and Reasoning categories.

E2.justification: v2 adds CLoud as an evaluated reward-model comparator on the original pointwise benchmarks and RewardBench. Table 10 also evaluates Prometheus-2-7B in both pointwise and pairwise modes. The original comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: Section 7.2 introduces a RewardBench protocol: score each response separately, compare the scores, and report preference accuracy. Table 10 additionally evaluates native pairwise Prometheus predictions. Existing benchmark protocols and Appendix A training and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 10 extends ablations A.1–A.4 to RewardBench, testing CoT source, loss/decoding choices, and second-stage initialization. Existing sensitivity, distribution-shift, inference-scaling, and appendix analyses remain. Section 6.3 removes the specific observation of frequent score-delimiter generation failures while retaining corrupted-CoT examples.

E5.justification: Both versions report four inference seeds and standard-deviation bands for the CoT-sampling experiment in Figure 3. v2 introduces no additional repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores remain unchanged. v2 adds CLoud correlations in Table 2, including average Pearson's r of 0.337, and extensive RewardBench results in Table 10. On RewardBench, RAFT achieves 0.775 average accuracy, exceeding TRACT's 0.736 and 0.748; CLoud achieves 0.759 and pairwise Prometheus 0.720. These are new-task findings rather than revisions to existing scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, predictor definitions, loss equations, and distribution-shift analysis are retained. v2 adds no formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v2 adds successful transfer from pointwise training to pairwise RewardBench evaluation as an explicit introductory contribution. The introduction and conclusion expand their superiority claims from four to five datasets; v1 described pairwise applications as future work. The central algorithmic contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 7 substantially discusses differences between rubric-based judges and reward models, interpreting CLoud's weak pointwise performance and TRACT's RewardBench performance as asymmetric transfer. A new Limitations section explicitly identifies dependence on output-probability access. These applicability arguments and qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Table 4 expands an abbreviated prompt template into explicit instructions and a complete input, reference answer, and rubric example. This is additional documentation, without evidence of changed experimental prompts. Hyperparameters, hardware, timings, access information, and licenses remain unchanged. Table 10's Llama-3-8B label conflicts with Section 4's Llama-3.1-8B specification.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds substantive positioning against CLoud and reward modeling, distinguishing training supervision, prediction heads, and rubric conditioning. Supporting additions include CLoud, RewardBench, and several reward-modeling references. The closed-source-judge paragraph and its OpenAI and Anthropic references are removed; the RAFT and self-distillation positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the abstract, introduction, and several discussion paragraphs, and updates affiliations. It inserts Section 7, Limitations, and Acknowledgments, renumbering related work and the conclusion. Most existing technical prose and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a CLoud row and a separate group for models trained on different data. Table 4 becomes a full-width worked example, and Table 10 is added. Several figures and appendix tables move, with more sparse appendix pages. Figures 1–3 themselves retain identical graphical content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evidence about applicability beyond pointwise judging and clarifies its relationship to the closely related CLoud approach, while documenting an explicit limitation and fuller prompt example. The benefit is limited by overextended claims: the conclusion asserts superiority across five datasets, although Table 10 shows RAFT at 0.775 above both TRACT variants, without discussing this exception. New checkpoint-label ambiguity also weakens reproducibility.
